sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯汀·

sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, in 2008, the Republican candidate for president campaigned on a plan to fight global warming.
sentences.zh: 今天，回顾2008年，当时的共和党总统候选人曾以应对全球变暖的计划作为竞选纲领。

sentences.en: How, in just nine years, the GOP has gone from combating climate change to arguing it doesn't exiSt. And the cities and states who say the U.S.
sentences.zh: 仅仅九年时间，共和党是如何从应对气候变化转变为否认其存在的？还有那些声称无论华盛顿如何，美国

sentences.en: will still meet its Paris commitment, with or without Washington.
sentences.zh: 都将继续履行巴黎协定承诺的城市和州。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, June 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月6日，星期二。

sentences.en: Coral Davenport, thank you for coming on.
sentences.zh: 科拉尔·达文波特，感谢你来到节目中。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Great to be with you as always, Michael.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你在一起，迈克尔。

sentences.en: So take us back to 2008.
sentences.zh: 那么，带我们回到2008年吧。

sentences.en: How were Republicans talking and thinking about climate change back then?
sentences.zh: 当时共和党人是如何谈论和看待气候变化的？

sentences.en: What was remarkable in 2008 is that the Republican candidate for the presidency, the GOP nominee, John McCain, was running on the strength of his climate change credentials.
sentences.zh: 2008年令人瞩目的一点是，共和党总统候选人、共和党提名人约翰·麦凯恩，正是凭借他在气候变化方面的资历作为竞选优势。

sentences.en: John McCain stood up to the president and sounded the alarm on global warming.
sentences.zh: 约翰·麦凯恩挺身而出对抗总统，并为全球变暖敲响了警钟。

sentences.en: Five years ago.
sentences.zh: 五年前。

sentences.en: He ran ads touting his own record of pushing climate change legislation in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他投放广告宣传自己在参议院推动气候变化立法的记录。

sentences.en: And in fact, it was very strong.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那份记录非常有力。

sentences.en: Reform.
sentences.zh: 改革。

sentences.en: Prosperity.
sentences.zh: 繁荣。

sentences.en: Peace.
sentences.zh: 和平。

sentences.en: John McCain.
sentences.zh: 约翰·麦凯恩。

sentences.en: Senator McCain had teamed with then-Senator Joe Lieberman on a major climate change bill in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 麦凯恩参议员曾与时任参议员的乔·利伯曼在参议院合作提出了一项重大的气候变化法案。

sentences.en: And around that time, we also saw several other Republican leaders stepping forward and kind of embracing climate change in a way that a lot of people don't remember.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间前后，我们还看到其他几位共和党领导人站出来，以一种许多人现在已经不记得的方式拥抱气候变化议题。

sentences.en: Newt Gingrich and Nancy Pelosi.
sentences.zh: 纽特·金里奇和南希·佩洛西。

sentences.en: We don't always see eye to eye, do we, Newt?
sentences.zh: 我们并不总是意见一致，对吧，纽特？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Did an ad together urging Congress.
sentences.zh: 一起拍了一则广告敦促国会。

sentences.en: But we do agree our country must take action to address climate change.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实同意，我们的国家必须采取行动应对气候变化。

sentences.en: We need cleaner forms of energy and we need them faSt.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更清洁的能源形式，而且我们需要尽快实现。

sentences.en: If enough of us demand action from our leaders, we can spark the innovation we need.
sentences.zh: 如果我们中有足够多的人要求领导人采取行动，我们就能激发所需的创新。

sentences.en: So what changed within the Republican Party and why did it change?
sentences.zh: 那么共和党内部发生了什么变化？为什么会发生这种变化？

sentences.en: So Obama gets elected.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马当选了。

sentences.en: You know, he thought climate change was an issue that he would be able to have bipartisan success with
sentences.zh: 你知道，他认为气候变化是一个他能够在国会获得两党支持并取得成功的议题，

sentences.en: in Congress, in part because the approach to tackling climate change that he wanted to take
sentences.zh: 部分原因是由于他想要采取的应对气候变化的方法，

sentences.en: had been basically invented and embraced by Republican economists and by his own Republican opponent
sentences.zh: 基本上是由共和党经济学家以及他在2008年的共和党对手约翰·麦凯恩所发明和采纳的，

sentences.en: in 2008, John McCain, the idea of cap and trade, which is placing a cap or limit on the pollution
sentences.zh: 即“限额与交易”的概念，也就是对污染设定上限或限制，

sentences.en: and creating a market where businesses can buy and sell permits to pollute, sort of a market solution.
sentences.zh: 并创建一个市场，让企业可以买卖污染许可，这算是一种市场解决方案。

sentences.en: So President Obama saw this as something that could get Republican buy-in, could get conservative buy-in, and he went ahead and brought this to Congress.
sentences.zh: 所以奥巴马总统认为这可以获得共和党的支持，可以获得保守派的支持，于是他将其提交给了国会。

sentences.en: In 2009, a cap and trade bill did pass the House.
sentences.zh: 2009年，一项“限额与交易”法案确实在众议院通过了。

sentences.en: So there was a sense this was going to be a possibility for a bipartisan victory.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有一种感觉，这可能成为两党合作的胜利。

sentences.en: And then a couple of things started to happen.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一些事情。

sentences.en: A big one that really sort of changed the story was the 2010 Supreme Court decision known as the Citizens United decision.
sentences.zh: 其中一件真正改变了故事走向的大事是2010年最高法院做出的裁决，即“联合公民”裁决。

sentences.en: Back now with news of a big change in American politics, one you will almost certainly see on your TV.
sentences.zh: 现在回到美国政治重大变革的新闻，这几乎肯定会出现在你的电视上。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: Supreme Court today overturned laws on the books for nearly a century and ruled that corporations can spend freely now on political campaigns.
sentences.zh: 最高法院今天推翻了实施近一个世纪的法律，裁定企业现在可以自由地在政治竞选中支出资金。

sentences.en: And one of the groups and companies that really stepped in and in a big way on that were the
sentences.zh: 而真正大规模介入其中的团体和公司之一就是

sentences.en: Koch brothers, Charles and David Koch, who run Koch Industries, which is sort of a large conglomerate organization that does a lot of oil refining, consumes a lot of fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 科赫兄弟，查尔斯·科赫和大卫·科赫，他们经营着科赫工业公司，这是一家大型企业集团，从事大量石油炼制，消耗大量化石燃料。

sentences.en: They're on the record questioning the science of climate change.
sentences.zh: 他们公开质疑气候变化的科学性。

sentences.en: I don't think science is settled.
sentences.zh: 我不认为科学定论了。

sentences.en: I mean, how could it be the people who are projected or who have these models?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那些做出预测或拥有这些模型的人怎么可能确定呢？

sentences.en: OK, if we do this, that other, we could be increased by one and a half degrees to four and a half or six.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果我们这样做，或者那样做，气温可能会升高1.5度到4.5度甚至6度。

sentences.en: The ocean could rise 20 feet or two feet.
sentences.zh: 海平面可能会上升20英尺或2英尺。

sentences.en: I mean, so it is not settled.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所以它并没有定论。

sentences.en: Matter of fact, science is never settled.
sentences.zh: 事实上，科学永远没有定论。

sentences.en: The sort of forum where this played out was in Republican primary races.
sentences.zh: 这种观点发酵的场所是在共和党的初选竞选中。

sentences.en: And Americans for Prosperity and other groups that were funded by the Koch brothers or by
sentences.zh: 而“繁荣美国”组织以及其他由科赫兄弟或科赫工业公司资助的团体，

sentences.en: Koch Industries would essentially go to these members of Congress and make it clear.
sentences.zh: 基本上会找到这些国会议员并明确表态。

sentences.en: There's a lot of talk about changing the Earth's temperature and a new tax called cap and trade.
sentences.zh: 关于改变地球温度和一项名为“限额与交易”的新税种，有很多讨论。

sentences.en: If you're in a Republican primary and you are talking about climate change, talking about
sentences.zh: 如果你在共和党初选中谈论气候变化，谈论

sentences.en: cap and trade, supporting any of these issues, we are going to pour all our resources into making sure that you don't get elected.
sentences.zh: “限额与交易”，支持这些议题中的任何一个，我们将投入所有资源确保你无法当选。

sentences.en: America can't afford the cap and trade tax.
sentences.zh: 美国负担不起“限额与交易”税。

sentences.en: Tell your senator to vote no.
sentences.zh: 告诉你的参议员投反对票。

sentences.en: And one example of this was Congressman Fred Upton.
sentences.zh: 其中一个例子就是国会议员弗雷德·厄普顿。

sentences.en: And I'm one that does believe that the planet is warming and we need to take steps to reduce it.
sentences.zh: 我确实相信地球正在变暖，我们需要采取措施减少这种变暖。

sentences.en: I think that we can.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以做到。

sentences.en: We can do it with greater efficiencies.
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过提高效率来实现。

sentences.en: Congressman Upton is a House member from Michigan.
sentences.zh: 厄普顿议员是来自密歇根州的众议员。

sentences.en: He's been in office for many years and for years he had a reputation as a real moderate who reached across the aisle and he sat on the powerful House Energy and Commerce Committee,
sentences.zh: 他任职多年，多年来一直以真正的温和派著称，能够跨越党派分歧，他还是众议院能源与商业委员会的成员，

sentences.en: which is the committee that writes energy and climate change laws.
sentences.zh: 该委员会负责制定能源和气候变化法律。

sentences.en: And he had been someone who on his on his website talked about climate change as a real problem.
sentences.zh: 他曾在自己的网站上谈论气候变化是一个真正的问题。

sentences.en: It was something that he talked about in his district.
sentences.zh: 这是他在选区谈论过的事情。

sentences.en: And Congressman Upton was also in line to become the next chairman of the House Energy Committee.
sentences.zh: 厄普顿议员当时也有望成为下一任众议院能源委员会主席。

sentences.en: So he was someone who would be very powerful in influencing the course of what would happen with climate change legislation.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个在影响气候变化立法进程方面非常有影响力的人。

sentences.en: He got a lot of messaging directly from Americans for Prosperity and from this growing Koch-funded
sentences.zh: 他直接收到了来自“繁荣美国”组织和这个日益壮大的科赫资助的

sentences.en: Tea Party wing that this will not fly.
sentences.zh: 茶党派系的大量信息，称这行不通。

sentences.en: And we will put up someone else in your primaries and we will make sure that you do not get this position.
sentences.zh: 我们会在初选中推举其他人，并确保你得不到这个职位。

sentences.en: And that sounds like a threat to basically take him out of office.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是要让他下台的威胁。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So what happened to Congressman Upton?
sentences.zh: 那么厄普顿议员后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: Did he win that re-election?
sentences.zh: 他赢得连任了吗？

sentences.en: He won the re-election and he won the chairmanship of the House Energy Committee.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了连任，也赢得了众议院能源委员会主席的职位。

sentences.en: And in order to win this powerful position in the House, Congressman Upton essentially had to denounce or walk back most of the views and positions that he held.
sentences.zh: 为了赢得众议院这个强有力的职位，厄普顿议员基本上不得不谴责或收回他所持的大部分观点和立场。

sentences.en: Is carbon a problem or isn't it?
sentences.zh: 碳是个问题吗？不是吗？

sentences.en: And if it is, if you're going to kill the EPA regulation, what's your solution?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，如果你要废除环保署的法规，你的解决方案是什么？

sentences.en: We want to do this in a reasonable way.
sentences.zh: 我们想以合理的方式来做这件事。

sentences.en: Before the end of the next decade, our country is going to need 30 to 40 percent more electricity than we use today.
sentences.zh: 在下个十年结束之前，我们国家需要的电力将比今天多出30%到40%。

sentences.en: So we need an all-of-the-above strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要一个“以上皆是”的策略。

sentences.en: We need clean coal.
sentences.zh: 我们需要清洁煤。

sentences.en: We need natural gas.
sentences.zh: 我们需要天然气。

sentences.en: We need nuclear, something that's not happened.
sentences.zh: 我们需要核能，这是目前还没实现的。

sentences.en: And we need a whole host of things.
sentences.zh: 我们需要各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: Do we need to regulate carbon?
sentences.zh: 我们需要监管碳排放吗？

sentences.en: I don't think that we have to regulate carbon to the degree where you have a carbon tax or you have a cap-and-trade system.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们必须监管碳排放到需要征收碳税或实行“限额与交易”系统的程度。

sentences.en: And the House spoke pretty loudly.
sentences.zh: 众议院的呼声非常响亮。

sentences.en: You know, you take that same cap-and-trade bill that passed the House last year, today it would lose by 50 votes and it could never come up in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，去年在众议院通过的那项同样的“限额与交易”法案，今天会以50票之差落败，而且它永远无法在参议院提出。

sentences.en: This is not the – this regulation process is not the way to proceed.
sentences.zh: 这不是——这个监管过程不是前进的方向。

sentences.en: He wiped out all mention of climate change from his website.
sentences.zh: 他从网站上抹去了所有关于气候变化的提及。

sentences.en: Just deleted it.
sentences.zh: 直接删除了。

sentences.en: Deleted it.
sentences.zh: 删除了。

sentences.en: It had been there before.
sentences.zh: 以前是有过的。

sentences.en: It wasn't there anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在没有了。

sentences.en: So, Coral, what exactly is the political calculation for a Republican seeking office in this period?
sentences.zh: 那么，科拉尔，这一时期寻求公职的共和党人的政治算计究竟是什么？

sentences.en: If you want the support, if you want the active, aggressive support of this unlimited resource of Koch Brothers money or Americans for Prosperity money,
sentences.zh: 如果你想要支持，如果你想要科赫兄弟或“繁荣美国”组织提供的无限资源支持，

sentences.en: you pretty much come out and say you oppose cap-and-trade, oppose climate change policy, and strongest of all say climate change isn't – human-caused climate change isn't real.
sentences.zh: 你基本上得站出来说你反对“限额与交易”，反对气候变化政策，最强烈地表态说气候变化不是——人类引起的气候变化不是真的。

sentences.en: The politics of this, which just two years before had been totally bipartisan, had all of a sudden become completely polarized.
sentences.zh: 这种政治局面，仅仅两年前还是完全两党共识的，突然之间变得完全两极分化了。

sentences.en: And climate change suddenly became this political litmus teSt.
sentences.zh: 气候变化突然成了政治试金石。

sentences.en: So, what ends up happening to the cap-and-trade bill?
sentences.zh: 那么，“限额与交易”法案最终结局如何？

sentences.en: It's easy to count to 60.
sentences.zh: 数到60票很容易。

sentences.en: I knew it.
sentences.zh: 我早就知道了。

sentences.en: I could do it by the time I was in eighth grade.
sentences.zh: 我在八年级的时候就能做到。

sentences.en: My point is this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是这样。

sentences.en: We know where we are.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们处于什么位置。

sentences.en: Harry Reid, who was the Senate Democratic leader at the time, said he couldn't even get enough support to bring the bill to the floor.
sentences.zh: 时任参议院民主党领袖哈里·里德表示，他甚至无法获得足够的支持将法案提交表决。

sentences.en: We know that we don't have the votes.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们没有足够的票数。

sentences.en: The bill just fell apart.
sentences.zh: 法案就这样流产了。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about President Obama, the man who beat Senator John McCain back in 2008.
sentences.zh: 让我们花点时间谈谈奥巴马总统，那个在2008年击败约翰·麦凯恩参议员的人。

sentences.en: How does his administration's approach to climate change in this period fit into the shifting Republican politics that you're describing?
sentences.zh: 他政府在这一时期应对气候变化的方法，如何融入你所描述的共和党政治转变中？

sentences.en: One of the things that President Obama did was he sat down with his advisers.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统所做的事情之一就是与他的顾问坐下来商讨。

sentences.en: They had several conversations where they said, all right, we understand that most of our legislative proposals that we bring to Congress will not get through.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了几次谈话，他们说，好吧，我们明白我们提交给国会的大多数立法提案都无法通过。

sentences.en: What can we do without Congress?
sentences.zh: 我们能在没有国会的情况下做什么？

sentences.en: And as it happened, climate change was one of the issues that they could take on without Congress.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，气候变化是他们可以在没有国会参与的情况下处理的议题之一。

sentences.en: There was enough authority in existing laws, specifically the Clean Air Act of 1970, to put forth regulations on carbon dioxide, planet warming emissions without going to Congress.
sentences.zh: 现有法律中有足够的授权，特别是1970年的《清洁空气法》，可以在不经过国会的情况下对二氧化碳和导致地球变暖的排放物实施监管。

sentences.en: If Congress won't act soon to protect future generations, I will.
sentences.zh: 如果国会不尽快采取行动保护子孙后代，我会采取行动。

sentences.en: So I will direct my cabinet to come up with executive actions we can take now and in the future to reduce pollution, prepare our communities for the consequences of climate change,
sentences.zh: 所以我将指示我的内阁提出我们现在和未来可以采取的行政措施，以减少污染，为我们的社区应对气候变化的后果做好准备，

sentences.en: and speed the transition to more sustainable sources of energy.
sentences.zh: 并加速向更可持续能源的转型。

sentences.en: The delivery of that message just played right into sort of the political moment of the time, which was already, you know,
sentences.zh: 这一信息的传达恰好迎合了当时的政治时刻，当时，你知道，
